text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Jan Smerek, president of steel maker VSZ, said his company planned to increase its exports to Japan from the current 5,000 tonnes of hot steel roles a year.
- Smerek said he had preliminary talks with unspecified Japanese firms over purchases of technology for modernising VSZ's main steel production and of lines for production of steel sheets.
- The National Property Fund (NPF), the state privatisation agency, has so far sold some 250 companies for about two billion crowns through direct sales of shares on the capital markets.

- The Antimonopoly Bureau last year assesed 127 cases of alleged violation of the competition law, but ruled that in only two cases did the accused break the law. Fines imposed by the Antimonopoly Bureau in 1996 totalled 3.13 million crowns.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar, during his visit to Japan, welcomed an offer from investment bank Nomura to continue managing inflow of Japanese investment to Slovakia.

- Meciar assured representatives of Nomura Securities Tokyo and Nomura International London that the two institutions still had the full confidence of the Slovak government despite a recent financial scandal in at the bank.
- The largest commercial bank, VUB, has called an annual shareholders' meeting for April 30.
- Steel producer Zeleziarne Podbrezova plans to invest 260 million crowns this year to modernise its main steel pipe production.

- Some 74 percent of all employees in the industrial sector worked for private firms at the end of last year. The private sector accounted for 86.2 percent of the workforce, with the trade and transport sectors accounting for 95.9 and 21.3 percent respectively.

PRAVDA - Opposition deputies, who have carried out an inspection in the NPF, said fund representatives have not ruled out the possibility that the two largest state-controlled banks, VUB and IRB, could be privatised just after the end of the privatisation embargo on March 31.

- The deputies said NPF had also not rulled out that the eventual sell-off of IRB and VUB could be carried out just by ruling of the fund's executive bodies, despite the fact that the constitutional court last year ruled that only the government was responsible for direct privatisation sales.
- President Michal Kovac repeatedly recommended to citizens to vote in favour of membership in NATO and of direct presidential elections in the forthcoming referenda on the questions.

- The army has officially introduced the 155-milimetre howitzer "Zuzana" into its forces, a move neccessary before Slovakia can start selling the unit abroad. The price on the world markets will be around $3.5 million.
